---
title: "Boost converter"
subtitle: "Power electronics"
toc: true
---

A boost converter steps a DC input up to a higher DC output by storing energy in an inductor while a switch is closed, then dumping it into the output (through a diode or synchronous switch) once it opens. Ideal CCM analysis again.

## Duty cycle

$$
D = 1 - \frac{V_{in}}{V_{out}}
$$

## Inductor current

While the switch is on, the full input voltage sits across the inductor, so ripple current is:

$$
\Delta I_L = \frac{V_{in} D}{f_{sw} L} \quad \Rightarrow \quad L = \frac{V_{in} D}{f_{sw}\, \Delta I_L}
$$

Unlike a buck, the inductor carries the *input* current, not the output current — this is why boost converters need bulkier inductors for the same output power. By power balance ($V_{in}I_{in} = V_{out}I_{out}$, ideal):

$$
I_{L,avg} = I_{in} = \frac{I_{out}}{1-D}
$$

## Calculator

```{=html}
<div id="boost-calc"></div>
<script src="../assets/js/calc-engine.js"></script>
<script>
Calc.create({
  root: "boost-calc",
  inputs: [
    { id: "Vin", label: "Vin (V)", value: 5, min: 0.01, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "Vout", label: "Vout (V)", value: 12, min: 0.01, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "fsw", label: "fsw (kHz)", value: 500, min: 1, step: 10 },
    { id: "Iout", label: "Iout (A)", value: 1, min: 0.001, step: 0.1 },
    { id: "ripplePct", label: "Ripple (% of IL,avg)", value: 30, min: 1, step: 1 }
  ],
  outputs: [
    { id: "D", label: "Duty cycle D" },
    { id: "ILavg", label: "IL,avg" },
    { id: "dIL", label: "ΔIL" },
    { id: "L", label: "L required" }
  ],
  compute: function (v) {
    if (v.Vout <= v.Vin || v.Vin <= 0) return { D: "invalid", ILavg: "-", dIL: "-", L: "-" };
    var D = 1 - v.Vin / v.Vout;
    var fsw = v.fsw * 1000;
    var ILavg = v.Iout / (1 - D);
    var dIL = (v.ripplePct / 100) * ILavg;
    var L = dIL > 0 ? (v.Vin * D) / (fsw * dIL) : 0;
    return {
      D: D.toFixed(3),
      ILavg: ILavg.toFixed(3) + " A",
      dIL: dIL.toFixed(3) + " A",
      L: (L * 1e6).toFixed(2) + " µH"
    };
  }
});
</script>
```
